title: LAPT-Scale: Scaling Embodied Policies with Latent Action Pre-Training on Human Videos

release_status.value: No dedicated official LAPT-Scale code or weight release verified from paper links and targeted search.

evidence_boundaries: LAM training uses 23.3K hours, policy pretraining 5.1K cleaned hours, scaling 1K/3K/5K; these are different quantities
Final policy outputs robot actions directly; LAM decoder is not required in deployed control
Continuous visual latent is not a physical joint-space command or human whole-body motion reconstruction
Stage 2 uses 250 hours robot alignment and Stage 3 uses additional task demonstrations
Real robot is AgiBot G1, not Unitree G1; tabletop manipulation does not validate locomotion or balance
Three original tasks use task-specific finetuning; four harder tasks share one multitask policy
Each real task-condition has 20 trials; independent-seed intervals not fully reported
Scaling improves average but Cup task falls from 95 to 75 percent between 3K and 5K
85 percent seen-domain success is tied with pi0.5 in the harder-task protocol
75 percent generalization average includes seen domain, not only OOD
Official pretrained DreamDojo scaling baseline differs from MSE-only diagnostic retrained on this corpus
VQ baseline does not establish universal superiority over all discrete tokenizers
Latent replacement and Stage-1 video rollouts are diagnostics, not robot-execution demonstrations
Exact policy backbone checkpoint, deployment frequency and embodiment-specific action fields not fully specified
Code, weights and complete data release not verified as of reading date
